description: Use consistent perspective (3/4 view or front-facing) with clear silhouette and bright contrasts
failure_mode: Inconsistent perspective → Meshy produces warped geometry or fails 3D reconstruction
mitigation: Use same perspective every generation. Seed images when possible for consistency. Include lighting from above-left for depth cues.

description: Style must be self-consistent: stylized, realistic, or cartoon — not mixed
failure_mode: Mixed styles → Meshy creates topologically inconsistent mesh; Mixamo rigging fails on unclear joint areas
mitigation: Commit to one style register per asset batch. Stylized/cartoony works better than photorealistic for AI 3D generation.

description: Characters must have visible separated limbs — T-pose or A-pose preferred
failure_mode: Hidden limbs or crossed arms → Mixamo cannot identify joint placement → rigging failure
mitigation: Prompt explicitly for T-pose or A-pose for character generation. Side-by-side limb visibility required.

description: Clean/transparent background strongly preferred
failure_mode: Busy background → Meshy includes background geometry in 3D model
mitigation: Prompt for flat color or transparent background. White background is acceptable.

description: For VFX effects (not characters): top-down or isometric angle preferred; clear geometry shape
severity: MEDIUM — VFX images are not the primary pipeline path (Unity VFX packs used instead)
failure_mode: Unclear VFX geometry → incoherent 3D model that cannot be used
mitigation: VFX are sourced from Unity Asset Store packs (Track B), not generated via ChatGPT→Meshy. ChatGPT→Meshy is for character/monster models only.

description: FBX or OBJ output required; USDZ/GLB/STL also supported
failure_mode: Output format incompatible with Mixamo import
mitigation: Use FBX for Mixamo pipeline. GLB for Blender cleanup if needed.
cost_estimate: Free tier: 100 credits/month; Pro: $20/mo (1k credits); ~20 credits per Meshy 6 generation

description: Output mesh quality varies — organic shapes (characters) generally better than hard-surface
failure_mode: Low-quality topology → Mixamo auto-rigger fails or produces poor deformation
mitigation: Use Meshy's retopology tool (Pro feature) to optimize polygon count. Target 5k-50k triangles for game-ready humanoid.

description: Meshy auto-rig detects humanoid vs non-humanoid automatically — must have clear head/torso/arm/leg topology
failure_mode: Non-humanoid mesh → cannot use Meshy or Mixamo rigging → full custom rig required
mitigation: Humanoid characters only for ChatGPT→Meshy→Mixamo pipeline. Monsters with non-humanoid forms require Blender custom rigging (separate workflow). This is a significant constraint for non-humanoid enemy generation.
cost_estimate: Additional Blender cleanup: ~$0 tool cost but hours of manual work

description: AI-generated textures may have baking artifacts or inconsistent style
failure_mode: Texture artifacts visible in game → reduces visual quality
mitigation: Meshy AI Texture Edit (Pro feature) allows texture revision. Blender material cleanup is also option.

description: Character must be approximately symmetrical for Mixamo auto-rigger — asymmetric characters will produce poor bone placement
failure_mode: Asymmetric mesh → bone placement error → joint deformation failure
mitigation: Ensure prompts produce symmetric characters. Post-process in Blender to mirror-fix if needed.

description: Mixamo supports HUMANOID BIPEDS ONLY — this is an absolute constraint with no workaround within Mixamo
failure_mode: Non-humanoid model → Mixamo rejects → 0 animations available from Mixamo library
mitigation: All characters in the ChatGPT→Meshy→Mixamo pipeline must be humanoid. Monster enemies with non-humanoid forms (spiders, dragons, etc.) need alternative rigging solution.

description: Character's feet must point forward (not sideways) at export — this is a documented Mixamo requirement
failure_mode: Sideways feet → incorrect bone orientation → animations play incorrectly
mitigation: Ensure generated characters have forward-facing feet. Check in Blender before Mixamo upload.

description: Character origin must be at X=0, Y=0, Z=0 before FBX export
failure_mode: Offset origin → character appears displaced in animation
mitigation: Standard FBX export practice. Set origin in Blender before export.

description: Mixamo has ~2500 total animations — combat/spell subset is limited compared to full library
failure_mode: Limited spell/dodge animations → visual repetition across many archetypes
mitigation: Supplement Mixamo with custom animations for key ARPG patterns (spell channel, charge-up, dodge roll). Mixamo provides base locomotion well; combat variants are thin.

description: Mixamo bones: Hips/Spine/Chest/Neck/Head/LeftUpperArm/LeftLowerArm/LeftHand/RightUpperArm/RightLowerArm/RightHand/LeftUpperLeg/LeftLowerLeg/LeftFoot/RightUpperLeg/RightLowerLeg/RightFoot
failure_mode: Bone name mismatch → Unity Humanoid Avatar setup required
mitigation: Use Unity's Humanoid Avatar system to remap Mixamo bone names. Standard workflow — well-documented.

description: Mixamo does NOT have weapon socket bones — weapon attachment requires Unity Animation Rigging or manual bone parenting at runtime
failure_mode: VFX that should attach to weapon or hand have no standard socket → manual parenting required
mitigation: Use Unity's Multi-Parent constraint or Animation Rigging package to attach VFX to hand/weapon bones at runtime. Attach VFX GameObject as child of RightHand bone.

description: Unity VFX packs use particle systems or VFX Graph — must attach to standard Mixamo bones (RightHand for cast effects, Body for auras, Ground for AOE)
failure_mode: VFX requires non-standard bone anchor → manual rigging setup per effect
mitigation: Design VFX attachment convention: (a) cast effects → RightHand bone; (b) aura/buff effects → Body/Chest bone; (c) AOE effects → ground-anchored (no bone parent). Document per asset.
time_estimate: ~30 min design once; 5 min per VFX attachment

description: VFX packs must match project render pipeline (Built-in vs URP vs HDRP) — many packs only support subset
failure_mode: Mismatched pipeline → VFX materials show pink/error — unusable without shader port
mitigation: Only procure VFX packs compatible with project's chosen render pipeline. URP is recommended for cross-platform mobile-first (Reincarnated) deployment. Filter procurement to URP-compatible packs.

description: Unity VFX packs designed at different scales — must verify scale compatibility with Mixamo humanoid (standard height ~1.8 Unity units)
failure_mode: VFX appears too large or too small relative to character
mitigation: Use scale multiplier on VFX prefab. Mixamo standard humanoid scale = approximately 1.8m height in Unity units. Test each VFX pack with reference character at session start.

description: Newer VFX Graph packs (like Summon Creatures Vol 1) require URP or HDRP — cannot use with Built-in pipeline
failure_mode: VFX Graph packs fail in Built-in projects
mitigation: If using Built-in pipeline: avoid VFX Graph packs. If using URP: both Particle System and VFX Graph packs work. URP recommended for Reincarnated.

description: Each VFX must be tagged with its canonical element (fire/water/earth/wind/lightning/holy/shadow/physical) for substrate-filtering at generation time
failure_mode: Missing element tags → wrong VFX spawned for wrong element kit → visual incoherence
mitigation: Maintain VFX element manifest (JSON/CSV) mapping Unity prefab name → element tag. Wire into engine substrate-filtering layer.
time_estimate: ~1 hour to create manifest; ~5 min per new pack added
